outcome.technical: stamp-verification.py: the cost table's figures are now read as slot-seconds and turned into wall time the way the sweep schedules them. New: load_sweep_table (costs plus the per-block figures; load_sweep_costs kept as a thin wrapper), sweep_jobs (the command's --jobs in either spelling, else the sweep's default_jobs rule: every core on CI=true, all cores but two elsewhere), schedule_wall (costliest first onto the least-loaded slot, the busiest slot's total), sweep_units, sweep_wall, wall_clause, proof_need (PROOF_RUNS = baseline, task, fix, times one run's wall), fit_problem, start_problem. sized_deadline now sizes from TIMEOUT_PER_COST times the proof's wall need (capped at MAX_TIMEOUT, never under the default) and carries wall/need even under --timeout. sweep_budget holds back one run's wall time (still capped at half the deadline) rather than the summed slot-seconds. run_red: fit_problem is checked before anything is built, and when the proof's runs need more than the deadline no run starts: could-not-prove, with a basis naming the wall need, how it was read and the deadline. start_problem runs before each of the baseline (owing baseline+task), task, task-held, second and fix runs, so a run left less than its measured need is not started and the basis says so, instead of a timeout the helper caused. Measured off the committed table: the P149.8-hwg command (test_run_test_gate + test_drive_phase) needs 1920s of wall time at 8 workers against a 565s deadline, so it is now refused up front; this task's own gate (test_stamp_verification) needs 198s and fits. tests/test_stamp_verification.py: new block swt-wall (_wall_cases, cases swt1-swt6, helpers _called and _spied_red); swc5/swc7/swd1/swd3/swd5 updated on purpose to the wall reading (swd3 and swc5 pass --jobs 4 so they do not depend on the host's core count; _SLOW_COST derived so the sized deadline stays just under the helper's default). Gate: `python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py tests/test_stamp_verification.py` exit 0, 1/1 files ok, 352 cases, run twice (the second after the final prose edits). `ruff check` on both files exit 0; `vermin -t=3.8-` exit 0; prose_number_claims, house_style_violations, path_preamble_violations, depth_sensitive_paths: no hits on either file. In-process mutants (each swaps one function on the loaded module, nothing written to the tree), then `_wall_cases` rerun: wall=sum -> swt1, swt2 red; fit never fires -> swt4, swt6; fit always fires -> swt4, swt5, swt6; start never fires -> swt5, swt6; start always fires -> swt5, swt6; --jobs ignored -> swt1, swt3; need counted as one run -> swt1, swt4; restored -> none red. That is not a defect; re-recording would add the figure.
